data.gender_notes: Richmond is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old English 'ric' meaning 'ruler, powerful' and 'hun' meaning 'rich, strong'. The name Richmond was popular during the Middle Ages and was often given to children born into noble families. The name Richmond carries the meaning “Strong, powerful ruler” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Richmond usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, powerful ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Richmond total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Richmond was the name of several historical figures and places throughout the Middle Ages, including a Norman nobleman and several English towns and cities. In modern times, the name has been popular in Virginia, USA. Richmond became the capital of the Virginia Colony in 1780 and played a significant role in the American Revolution. The name was also given to numerous schools, churches, and other institutions in the United States and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: As a Christian name, Richmond holds the potential for a deep spiritual meaning. 'Rich' in this context can refer to the spiritual wealth that comes from a close relationship with God. The name invites those who bear it to aspire to godly rulership and to live richly in the blessings of God's grace and guidance. The name also carries the echo of the biblical promise in Matthew 6:20, that those who store up treasure in heaven shall be rich indeed. In summary, the name Richmond offers a powerful reminder of the spiritual riches that come from cultivating a deep, meaningful connection with God.
